summary: Mason County, WA peak in Olympic National Park; a 1930s cabin may have stood here and is now gone; Willhite found no evidence of one between the summits.

facts.status_note: Register and firelookout.com say the 1930s cabin is gone; Willhite found no evidence of a cabin between the summits and does not know whether a lookout was built

access.note: Hiking route from the Staircase Ranger Station in Olympic National Park; no trail on the upper mountain

visit.trail_note: Hiking distance 5.5 miles one way (Willhite); trail ends at about 2,650 feet, and the upper mountain has no trail

events.note: Scouting climb on July 18, 1935 by Robert H. Mealey; the report recommended the peak as a lookout site
Forest Lookouts lists the site as activated June 20, 1942, Olympia Filter Center; the page does not describe the use

corrections.why: Firelookout.com, Forest Lookouts and Willhite all place Mount Lincoln in Olympic National Park. Only the register says Olympic National Forest. Confirm with the National Park Service before publishing.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com say a 1930s cabin existed and is now gone. Willhite says it is not known when or if a lookout was built, and found no evidence of a cabin between the north and south summits.
The register says Olympic National Forest; firelookout.com, Forest Lookouts and Willhite say Olympic National Park. The record is corrected to the park (see corrections).

notes_for_editor: Whether any lookout or cabin was built is unresolved: the register and firelookout.com say a 1930s cabin existed and is gone; Willhite says it is unknown. No built event is recorded for that reason. The agency correction (National Forest to National Park) rests on three pages against one; verify with NPS. The register's FFLOS registration date (Jan 17, 2012) was not visible in the text read, so no fflos_registered event. Brief elevation (1787 m) left as is; Willhite gives 5,868 ft for the summit.
